note: Body Dao's home tier licenses no humanoid, so this congregation is assembled entirely from visitors who pay the gate fee, and its annual observance is the only fixed date the plains hold.
The only worked face within reach of the ford, which is what lets a faith charge its initiation in ore rather than in a currency the tier does not have.
The vein is shut because a generation opened a living core to see whether a higher gate would fit, and the prohibition that answers that failure is this faith's entire content.
A rite needs a second party to be a rite rather than a demonstration, so what is pressing below the seam is addressed as a party rather than denied as a substance.
Cement is the fee and the fee is the institution, so the whole congregation is a claim on one exhausted deposit and the deposit's rate of fall is a matter of public record.
A culturer still eats, and the tier's only remedy is also its most contested mouthful, so the temple keeps a store it is not permitted to fence.
The faith is taught inside the commons and takes the commons's grain as part of its fee, which makes it a practice of a village rather than a building with a door.
The plurality of the congregation and the body the rite was worked out among; nothing in a sealed socket identifies what was sealed.
A furnace body needs the seal more urgently and supplies most of the Binders, which is the clearest case in the setting of a faith whose priesthood is held by the race it is least suited to.
A dense body cements easily and is not served by the rite, so the stone-born attend out of the surrounding commons rather than out of need.
A body that metabolises qi out of the dead is the one congregation the burial rite does not frighten, since what is recovered at a burial is exactly what they already work.
Preservation through form is the only reading a three-slot frame can legibly support, so the faith and its Dao are not two positions but one position with and without a building.
Both close the furnace permanently and both forbid showing off, but one returns the body's ore to a public forge and the other returns nothing at all, so no household has ever belonged to both.
Two body-path certainties about permanence stand on the same ground and have never spoken, because one charges for a seal and the other regards every purchase as a concession.
The temple owns the only forge that can seal and the only certification a gate-test accepts, so the caste is controlled by the institution it makes indispensable.
A three-slot frame with no spatial law is why a burial has to be a recovery operation: ground here cannot be returned to, so the body has to go back to the forge instead.
Its congregations sit where the gate fee is charged, because its first public act every period is refusing the gate-fee crowd and going home.
Both refuse the ledger as the condition of belonging, and a paperless people on the spirit tier who will not accept exclusivity is the same argument made by people who cannot write.
A carrying culture that abandoned its price list four centuries ago and an assembly that forbids naming a debt are the same rule enforced by custom and by statute.
The body the practice was worked out among, and the body that most often finds itself without a certificate to publish.
A long-lived perception body is the one most able to produce a figure it would rather not publish, which is the Assembly's only admission test and therefore its natural membership.
The belief is the reason the Assembly can exist at all: it is the only afterlife claim in the setting that a six-group law budget actually permits, so it has no supernatural liability to defend.
A congregation that forbids a ledger and a creator cannot produce a genesis, so it occupies the myth slot and performs a festival in order to decline to say anything at all.
The prohibition is the Assembly's founding clause, written down as law precisely so that it cannot be quietly abandoned when a member is in trouble.
One institution may certify a body and one refuses to certify anybody, and neither can exist on the same ground because the second makes the first's monopoly meaningless.
The cost of the Assembly's refusal to hold a grave is written into its own law: whoever excludes somebody ends up burying them, in that person's name.
The counting houses' refusal to publish a price is what makes the Assembly's prohibition survivable in practice, since no counterparty can cite the one record it forbids.
The only crossing of the Sixfold Ridge, and the only ground in the setting where an unbuyable calendar has to be obeyed by an armed institution.
A border with five of six laws seated and the sixth deliberately left unwritten has no season in it, so it has to be held by hand all year by people paid to stand on it.
Mind Dao teaches that the self can leave a body; the Vigil's entire roster is people who cannot leave, and a garrison told it has an exit is a garrison that uses it.
With no elemental seat there is nothing to anchor a year, so the faith's whole calendar is a flock arriving, and a doctrine had to be invented around an animal's itinerary.
The god is kept rather than addressed: the pass opens when the birds come and closes when they have gone, which is the only scheduling authority a five-seat frame can supply.
The plurality of the households on the ridge, conscripted by rotation and owed nothing by the faith but the roster.
A dense body stands a long watch better than anything else here, which is why the rotation's hardest hours are filled by stone-born who volunteered for them.
The perception race reads the flock's arrival earlier than anyone else, and the Vigil's date is set by the birds, so their judgement is the only thing that matters here.
The prohibition is the faith's content: no account of the self leaving a body, in any form, enforced by a duty roster that is a distributed readership.
The sheds are paid for out of the rotation and exist only to hold the people the rotation sends, so the faith owns them in the only way the ridge recognises.
The holder of the crossing collects and sets a price and never a date; the Vigil supplies the Keepers who make collecting defensible, and neither can function without the other.
The same households cut and maintain the crossings they stand on, and a builder's mark is renewed on the evening of a death for the same reason a Keeper's shift is not.
Ten seats over six law groups leave four duplicates that can never be filled, and the only authority that can be built without filling them is one that treats vacancy as a state.
The decree made vacancy a writable condition; the faith is what that condition grew a theology around once it turned out nobody was ever going to fill them.
An unfillable seat is addressed as a titled entity with a calendar and no holder, because a seat nobody speaks to is indistinguishable from a seat that does not exist.
The Empty Chair rite can only continue the calendar honestly if the office is the durable thing, which makes waiting the only afterlife that supports the institution.
The rite is the faith's whole annual behaviour: the chair is emptied, the entry stays open and the calendar is not interrupted, so a death at court is never a stoppage.
A four-century lifespan is the body that can hold a register entry for longer than the office's successor chain, so the clerks are drawn from it.
The clerks' second body, admitted on the same terms, and the reason the register is not simply a longmarrow private keeping.
The church owns no ground and no ore; its whole capital is the standing to certify that a seat is empty, which the decree made into a thing worth holding.
Nine vacant seats at the top and four below with no procedure able to certify any of them empty is the condition the theology was written to describe.
The school holds that vacancy is arithmetic and refuses memorial vocabulary for the Refused Seating; both readings are kept on file at the court for that reason.
Ten law slots cannot fill from six groups, so four seats here are surplus rather than shortage, and a religion arose from the arithmetic before anyone did.
The Regency may name a seat and may not take one, which is exactly the rule the faith treats as piety rather than as an oversight.
Fifteen imprints over three layers is the only composition in the setting with real slack, and it is the only place a law can be held apart from its effect and read.
The rite is the faith: one clerk, one act of attention, no instrument, no second participant and nobody authorised to organise the next one.
The faith has no other office and the clerks have no other master, which is what lets the dissolution clause be absolute without a second body to enforce it.
Nine of the fifteen imprints are surplus duplicates over three layers, so the third layer holds the only genuine spare volume in the setting.
The College keeps the floor and the room while the clerks hold the observation, and neither may take the other's function, because a floor-tender who watches is a second clerk.
Bodies go into the third layer where there is surplus, and the clerks are the only people who know what the layer is currently doing, so burial becomes a favour to the next observation.
An elemental body needs a world that seats element, and only the two highest tiers do, so the congregation is present exactly where the law concentration makes it possible at all.
A body with no unmediated interior left cannot take the mind path, so the one race that cannot do this work is the one that staffs the room around the person doing it.
A clerk's lifespan is a rounding error on a clock running ten to a hundred times a mortal's, so the office is a one-use body and the body is the fee.
The splinter keeps the discipline and drops the dissolution, so the one clause the parent regards as the whole of the institution is the clause the splinter refused.
Its congregations are the ones the Sealed Core could not charge, which makes the largest faith on the tier the one that exists because of what the largest temple costs.
A third of the Core's congregations could not pay the initiation fee in worked ore and were told the rite was closed to them.
It performs the same cement in the same public forge with the priest's words left out, and the omission is the whole of its heresy.
It attends the annual observance and does not seal, standing at the back, which is the closest the two congregations have come to anything.
The cinder works because ore holds qi and the ceremony is a mechanism rather than a promise, which is the only thing this congregation asserts.
The furnace bodies the Sealed Core's fee excluded first are the largest single group here, and they attend the cinder without paying for anything.
A long-lived perception body is over-represented among people who can afford no initiation, because an expensive rite prices out exactly the people who live longest.
The plurality, and the group whose absence from the Sealed Core's register is the split's own evidence.
One says the rite is a mechanism and the other says it is not even a repair; both agree nothing is sealed, and they still refuse to share a building.
The first tier with humanoids is the first tier where a child can be taught something, and the first where the teacher may legally not be from the tier at all.
Body Dao's home tier licenses no humanoid, so every teacher of it on the plains is a visitor collecting a gate fee, and a doctrine delivered by a non-resident is a tariff rather than a truth.
It makes the census a teaching prerequisite rather than a scholarly finding, so the one document that proves a Dao is non-native is the document every child meets first.
A dense body cannot take the mind path and is taught nothing by the top tier's factions, so the population with nothing to gain from a Dao is the population that reads the census.
The plurality among the taught, and the race the mortal tier produces in every household but licenses nowhere.
A perception-built body reads a strained qi more finely than anything else here, which makes it the only body for which knowing the composition before choosing a path is worth anything.
The only academy that teaches by seating a law and diffing what the tier newly permits, which is exactly the exercise the Writ makes compulsory before any path is named.
It publishes a reading list and no exclusivity, which is why the petition about graded cloth names a house that publishes technique and discretion and never names this one.
It exists because the court permits both registers, and a splinter with no seat of its own can only be registered where the seat it disputes is.
The Ledger's benediction of a vacancy is a fee nobody can refuse once they have started attending, and a denomination that performs nothing has to say so out loud.
It holds the Refused Seating to be arithmetic rather than tragedy, which makes it the only congregation that can say what happened without a memorial vocabulary.
The court it sits in is run from two tiers below Mind Dao's home, and a sect that reduces every question of intent to a dial reading is structurally the mind reading with the metaphysics removed.
It forbids naming a vacancy aloud because the reading is a comfort sold to the anxious; the Church of Names answers that comfort is not the objection and continues to hold it.
Clerks at the immortal court are visitors on the same terms as everyone else, which is why a splinter of the office's own religion is held by the body with no standing in it.
A body that cannot leave the brine line is a body whose obligation to a seat cannot be discharged in person, which the sect reads as the seat's problem and the saltfolk read as theirs.
Every appointment passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, so the rule that no one may take a seat by decree is what lets a sect that forbids all ceremony stand at the court at all.
The only ground in the setting where a body can be held against fifteen imprints, and the only ground where a congregation can carry a standing upkeep bill.
A clerk completed an observation and then declined to let the office dissolve, which is the single clause the parent faith exists to enforce.
Holding one position against fifteen imprints is the top-tier reading of spatial and temporal law performed without the metaphysics, so the sect is a faith that has become a technique.
The oath was honoured once and then a second hour was begun anyway, which the parent faith reads as proof the oath was never the problem and the dissolution clause was.
A population that draws its qi from one resonator and stops without it is the only body in the setting for whom being permanently non-portable is not a defect but a condition of office.
A fragment is worthless before its owner is and a standing office is a liability, so the sect is the one congregation whose asset gets cheaper while it holds on.
Six seats against exactly six groups is the first frame where nothing is merely missing, and it is therefore the first place the arithmetic of the whole setting can be taught in one room.
It holds that the three readings are tools adopted by standing in a frame, which is the dao variable's own claim stated without a hierarchy to be loyal to.
All three Daos present their reading as the way a world is shaped into rather than as a choice; the school treats that as a claim about standing and refuses to hold any of the three permanently.
Qi Dao is allied with Mind Dao and holds ground rather than running a school, so the one party that can explain why its own reading works is one nobody has thought to tax.
Mind Dao is native to the tier that runs ten to a hundred times a mortal's clock, and a school that makes the whole ladder adoptable is the standing negation of a reading that claims to be home.
A species the world permitted without inscribing cannot cultivate and belongs to no culture; a school with no lineage and no inheritance is the one institution it can hold without being asked to.
A body that must settle on a path early is the body that most needs to know the path is a tool and most resents being told so.
It makes the census its entire curriculum and refuses any sentence of the form a Dao holds true everywhere, which is why the factions that hold ground teach nothing.
The Vigil's refusal to admit it to the ridge is recorded by the school as a result rather than an injustice, because a school that argued would be arguing for a lineage.
The ground named for the frame that first seated every group at once is where the one classroom runs, unseated and unendowed.
A universe is six groups that exist once and whole; the school's whole claim is that this is a closed budget and every seventh-law doctrine is arithmetic error rather than mystery.
Seat the last missing law, diff what the tier newly permits, and record which result caused which; the finding is negative and it is the school's entire curriculum.
It runs the one permitted test of the prohibition, in a test frame, because a prohibition nobody may test is a superstition rather than a proof.
The descendants are the only people alive who watched a law change from inside a body, which is the only qualification the classroom admits.
The frame somebody tried to build by seating a seventh law in a vacant slot is kept as a record precisely so the school can hand a student the failure instead of a warning.
The diff the school teaches is what makes the heresy visible, and the school does not endorse it and is asked about it perhaps once a decade.
Forty years of measured fall with no further cavity is the only evidence the congregation has that what is below the worked-out seam is still there and still pressing.
An appetite needs a name and the name needs a grievance, and the grievance is the only event in the setting's record that every holder of the ore agrees on.
A god with a face could be bargained with and an appetite cannot, which is why the temple's inner wall is left bare with the reason written on it in the congregation's own hand.
One doctrine puts purpose under the ground and the other puts nothing anywhere; both are held by people who work the same face and refuse to discuss it.
A three-slot world seats no spatial law, so nothing opens a cavity and the pressure below the seam cannot be relieved by any amount of digging.
A pressure held sacred only where the deposit is worked out, because a seam still being dug has no appetite to be fed.
A vacancy at this tier is a physical absence visible from the district below, so somebody has to stand in front of it once a period and say the word.
The court enters it at the head of every list of seats it keeps, which is the only formal precedence anything in the setting holds.
Four duplicated imprints in the second layer are the whole of its evidence: there is a place for the group to sit twice and nowhere for a seventh to sit at all.
The annual reading exists because a vacancy never spoken aloud cannot be told apart from an absence, which is the exact failure the Refused Seating left behind.
The god is an office, and the only deity in the setting with an ordinal in its name and no holder.
The unfilled ledger's nine high seats and four below are the shape this deity's calendar maps onto.
The office that names the unfilled seats and is forbidden to take them is the body whose entry this deity is, so the notary and the god are the same fact in two registers.
The setting's only authored climate, and the one place where a recurring arrival could be mistaken for a season by somebody who had not checked whether elemental law was seated.
The flock occupies the worst hours of the crossing and it recurs on its own, so an animal's itinerary is the only calendar on a ridge with no season.
The pass is opened when the birds come and closed when they have gone, and the holder of the toll has never once been able to set a date.
A bird on a schedule is not a person, so there is no prayer and no offering, and the faith's god is kept rather than addressed.
The window is a quota set by the Tidemark season rather than the holder's preference, which is the arrangement this deity makes possible and the toll defends.
Six slots with element deliberately left unwritten is the condition that removes the anchor, and a bird's arrival is the substitute the ridge built instead.
The tier licenses no humanoid, so the caste that certifies every breakthrough taken here is drawn entirely from the population the frame classes as a visitor.
The caste is closed because a second seal is forbidden, which makes it hereditary in practice without any law requiring it and no admission anyone outside could clear.
A Binder is the only person authorised to seal and the only person who has sworn never to unseal, which is the whole design of both halves of the office.
The Reckoning Seat certifies a breakthrough by a body the tier is not licensed to produce, and it cannot pay a Binder or replace one, so the certification runs the other way.
Furnace bodies supply most of the caste because they need the seal most urgently, which is why the priesthood of a temperate faith is staffed by the race that cannot keep it.
Commonborn binders are the plurality, and they are the ones who close permanently too, so the caste's ethics belong to bodies the rite was not written for.
A Binder cannot be buried by the temple; they are recovered as inventory with their own consent not required, which is the office's price and is in the oath.
The lodge sells bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, while the caste's certification decides who is sound enough to attempt one, and neither will sell to the other.
One clerk per observation, seated for the observation and dissolved at its end, and no mechanism exists to record who was seated.
The oath is what makes a silence legible as an observation rather than as an absence, and it is the only reason the office produces anything worth recording.
Fifteen seats against six laws with a clock running ten to a hundred times a mortal's is why an observation that must be repeated costs more lifetimes than the tier has.
A body holding more life than its law has room to inscribe reaches the twenty-ninth gate and nobody has come back, which is the shape of the clerk's office at its limit.
A four-century body is the only one in the setting whose lifespan is comparable to the work, and the clerks are drawn from it for exactly that reason.
Nine of the fifteen imprints are surplus duplicates over three layers, so the third layer is where a law can be held apart from its effect and read.
The splinter sat down twice, and the office exists on the rule that nobody does, which the parent faith now treats as the only clause that was ever load-bearing.
The faith holds no thing at all; it holds a duty with a roster, and the roster is the entire institution.
A conscripted congregation cannot be asked for voluntary constancy, so the oath is what the rotation is actually made of and it is short enough to say over a mouthful of water.
The keeper collects nothing and the holder of the crossing collects, and the keeper's presence is what makes collecting defensible rather than extortionate.
The one standing force on the plains is a queue-management company at a stair; the ridge's own force exists because a keeper who may refuse would be exactly that, and so may not.
A cold-climate body that reaches far and never stays there is the one race whose natural cycle matches a rotation, so the ridge's off-season keepers are long-winters.
A body built to occupy ground that is water half the time and land the other is the one population that does not object to a shed standing on it.
One adult per household per rotation, with a two-rotation bar on giving twice, which is the whole of the roster and the whole of the ridge's staffing.
The prohibition only has force where a socket exists to be sealed, so it is a mortal-tier rule with no meaning anywhere else.
It is the whole content of the faith: no socket may be opened once sealed, and the temple forge is built so that it cannot do the other thing.
A generation opened a living core to see whether a higher gate would fit, the vein has been shut ever since, and this prohibition is the answer written down so it cannot be tried again.
Enforcement is the caste's refusal to certify an unsealed body, so the prohibition is not a rule with a penalty but a wall with nobody left who can open it.
The omission of the priest's words makes the same operation a repair rather than a rite, and the temple has never formally answered which of the two it thinks that is.
A seal that is never opened cannot be known to hold, so the annual observance exists to answer the question the prohibition itself creates.
The one tier where a written claim can be made enforceable across a whole road network, and therefore the only place where the prohibition needs to be written down at all.
No debt owed by a named person may be published, and the prohibition binds the Assembly's own members before it binds anyone else.
The Saltledger answers access with a ledger; the Assembly forbids the ledger and cannot use one in a dispute, so neither will say the other's name in an argument.
The counting houses' refusal to publish a price is what makes the prohibition survivable, since the one record a party might cite does not exist in writing.

A thing entirely real only while it is being misremembered has no body and copies itself out of other people's recollection, so an institution that forbids the written record is the one place it cannot be listed.
An assembly that forbids the ledger cannot shelter anybody, so the law requiring the excluder to bury is what an unenforceable prohibition leaves behind.

Fifteen imprints over three layers is where a law can be pressed into one held value instead of spread, and it is the only composition in the setting with the slack to attempt the seated lesson at all.
The attempt consumed a slot on an absence and afterwards cannot be told from an empty one, so the failure is now a certificate no instrument in the setting can issue.
A name rather than a place, kept as a record, is the material the lesson is built on: the student is handed the failure instead of a warning.
The order that would have to be seated is the same fact the setting has censored, so the prohibition and the missing record are two halves of one hole.
A slot is one law at one value in one layer, which is why the refusal can be taught as arithmetic rather than only as a prohibition.
The prohibition holds only where the duty roster is, and the roster is a distributed readership with no room in which an account can circulate unreported.
No account of the self leaving a body in any form, because such an account is a recruiting promise made to people with one road and a rotation they already owe.
Mind Dao's reading needs spatial law at the top of its range, so its practitioners are the only bodies who can leave, and the Vigil's entire garrison is the set of people who cannot.
Both use a standing practice at a boundary rather than a word, and the ridge's version forbids the sentence the top tier's culture treats as its whole content.
A mind-path heresy tested somewhere the Vigil's ban cannot reach is the one hole in the prohibition, and nobody on the ridge is permitted to say where.
Ore from the temple's own face, a socket opened and cemented in the public forge, and the amount entered in the register.
The only initiation in the setting whose fee is a physical deposit, so the faith's growth rate is a measurable function of what is left in the ground.
Same forge, same ore, same column of the register, with the single difference that nobody is watching for a result at a burial.
The annual observance is this rite run against the whole book at once, which is how a seal that is never opened gets checked at all.
The denomination performs the same cement with the priest's words removed, and the omission is what makes it heresy rather than a second tradition.
The rite and the prohibition are the same fact seen from two sides, and the temple's forge is built so that only one of them can be performed.
One clerk, one act of attention, held until it ends, and nobody permitted to organise the next one.
The only layer with surplus imprints is the only place a law can be held apart from its effect and read rather than obeyed.
The College tends the floor and keeps the room and may not observe, because a floor-tender who watches is a second clerk by another name.
A half-completed hour must not be reportable afterwards, and the oath that forbids answering during it is the only thing that makes the silence mean anything.
Fifteen imprints pressed into one held value rather than spread across three layers is the same fact this rite performs one held act at a time.
The rite cannot be scheduled and cannot be inherited, and a clerk who found a way to sit down twice is the entire origin of the splinter.
The pass opens when the birds come and closes when they have gone, which is the only observance a conscripted congregation can be asked to attend.
Every Keeper rotation is scheduled against the passage, so the roster and the rite are the same document.
The one calendar nobody can buy is the one everybody obeys, which is the whole reason a toll with no timetable is defensible.
The flock occupies the worst hours of the crossing and recurs on its own, so an animal's itinerary is the only calendar this frame can supply.
Six slots with element deliberately left unwritten removes the anchor a year would hang on, and an animal's recurrence is what the ridge built instead.
Both intertidal communities read a recurring arrival off the ground rather than off a calendar, and both treat the reading as the record.
The dead are opened within the day, the socket's contents recovered to the temple forge and the amount entered against the name.
Ground here cannot be returned to, so a grave is one more thing that stays, and forty decades of spoil on the seam floor is the same fact at a larger scale.
Recovery only has material to work with where the ore was, and the register column records the amount precisely so the deposit's rate of fall stays public.
One keeps everything and returns it; the other keeps nothing and returns nothing, and the two rites cannot be performed by the same household for the same body.
At a settlement funeral the dead are read as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, and the temple's register is a second census the court does not control.
A people who metabolise qi out of the dead are near every graveyard in the setting, and on their ground this rite and ordinary scavenging are indistinguishable.
Spatial law unwritten is why waste does not disperse here, which is what makes recovery a moral duty rather than a tidy-up.
No preparation, no site, no marker and one spoken line that is not written down, because the prohibition on named records does not stop at death.
Nothing disperses on ground that seats no spatial law, so a body left unmarked stays, and staying is the practical objection the rite has to survive.
A rite that cannot hold a grave cannot shelter anybody, so the law requiring the excluder to bury is what the absence leaves behind.
On ground where carrionfolk work an unmarked body is gone within a day, and the Assembly reads that as the rite completing itself rather than as a failure.
A paperless people who will not accept exclusivity already had to invent an ending that leaves nothing behind, and the Assembly adopted theirs.
A belief with nothing after it needs a rite with nothing left over, and the Assembly's two doctrines are the same refusal stated in two registers.
The chair is emptied, the entry stays open and the calendar is not interrupted, so a death at court is never a stoppage.
The chair stays in the district below where it can be seen, because an office that cannot be seen empty is indistinguishable from one that does not exist.
Every appointment passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, so an office outlives its holder by construction and the rite has something to continue.
The Regency may name a seat and may not take one; the rite exists to keep the register moving without anyone being promoted into a vacancy by decree.
A seat that has never been occupied is named at the Seat Quiet rather than mourned, and the difference between the two states is the faith's whole content.
The notary names the unfilled seats and is forbidden to take them, and the chair stays open because the office that would fill it is structurally unable.
Whoever excludes a person accepts the duty of burying them, in that person's name, in writing, at the exclusion's own expense.
On the plains a name can be culled from every household ledger, so this entry survives only because its author did not benefit from writing it.
Houses that could not fund an ascent culled their own branches, so the population of the plains is full of people whose line was cut and whose exclusion nobody had to record.
A line with no household willing to admit it and a founding bar no pairing clears is exactly the case this law was written for, and it is the only record such a person ever gets.
The Assembly performs no grave at all, so where it excludes somebody the burden passes to a community that never agreed to it, which is the price of having no shelter.
The two cover every way a person can end up without a place: one holds a seat open and the other holds nothing, and neither can be abolished quietly.
Every body goes down to the third layer because the surface is reserved for the standing and the held, and a body at the surface obstructs an observation.
Nine of the fifteen imprints are surplus duplicates over three layers, so the third layer holds the only genuine spare volume anywhere in the setting.
The clerks are the only people who know what the third layer is currently doing, which makes them the sole authority the faith recognises anywhere.
Every burial makes the next observation marginally easier, which the faith records without comment and which is the closest it comes to a doctrine of merit.
One puts bodies where nothing comes back and the other puts them where nothing was kept, and only one of the two leaves a place a person can be shown.
Fifteen imprints need three layers, so the composition that makes the observation possible is the same one that makes somewhere to put a body possible.
Not annihilation and not continuation: the question has no referent, because a self that ends has nothing to continue into.
A universe is the closed budget of six groups that exists once and whole, and a place to arrive in would be another frame carrying a seventh group.
One says dead cores resume work and the other says there is nowhere for them to resume into, and if the Court is right a measurable amount of it is happening right now.
The rival keeps power with the dead rather than work, and a person waiting on a seat is not judged, not gone and not at rest.
A slot is one law at one value in one layer, and six groups cannot fill fifteen slots, which is the arithmetic the whole argument leans on.
The lowest tier spends three of six groups, so a person here has the fewest groups to survive into and the Assembly's claim is at its least exotic.
The one recorded attempt to make a frame that does not exist is the strongest available evidence that no second frame is available either.
Death ends the person and not the core, which is what makes returning the material at burial an honest operation rather than an abandonment.
The tier's only dense material is the ore a core can be caged in, so a doctrine about what the dead do is also the setting's only workable account of where the metal goes.
The register records how much was recovered, and a faith that claimed the person had survived would be caught out at the first audit, so the belief resolves the audit instead.
A measurable amount of resumed work and a universe that offers nowhere to resume into are the same doctrine with and without a supply chain behind it.
A body is fuel and the dead are fuel not yet spent, which is the only reason the deposit's rate of fall can be discussed as a moral question rather than a commercial one.
One keeps the dead's work and the other the dead's office, and neither register at the court will accept the other's claim about what survives.
A person is not judged but waited for, and a dead officeholder is entered as pending rather than as finished.
The chair has to stay open and the calendar has to keep moving, which is only honest if the office is the durable thing rather than the officeholder.
The court runs five to fifty times a mortal's clock, so an unsettled obligation is inherited by successors rather than discharged by the person who incurred it.
Nine vacant seats at the top and four below produced an authority built entirely out of vacancies, and that authority needs the dead to keep standing in its ledger.
Waiting on a seat is neither judgment nor release, and the Assembly's claim that the question has no referent is aimed directly at this one.
A seat unfilled for two generations because its heirs were culled is the form this doctrine takes in the lower polity, where a line rather than a surplus is the reason.
Nobody made anything; a world is opened by paying out of a fixed supply of six groups, and whoever paid could afford three seats.
Somebody had to pay to open a world at all, the bill was written in law seats, and every tier since is a receipt for the same payment.
A slot spent on an absence is money spent on nothing, which is the one transaction a fiscal myth cannot forgive and therefore the one it makes a sin.
A slot is one law group at one value in one layer, so the budget counts imprints rather than laws, and that is why the supply runs out before the vocabulary does.
The three-slot frame the payment bought is still running on that arithmetic, which is why the plains have no season, no clock and no distance.
The school teaches the diff that shows the myth is arithmetically true, and the myth is what a congregation can sing while the school can only demonstrate.
One says a world was paid for and one says there was no first anything, and both are performed on the same night one hour apart so nobody attends only one.
There is no first event; any account that opens with one is a list of items given a first line for the convenience of reading.
Both are creation myths performed at the same hour, and the disagreement is about whether a world that exists owes anybody anything.
The same night as the tithe, one hour apart, so that anybody who wants to hear only one of them has to choose which to walk away from.
A sentence of the form something began always implies somebody who was owed, which is the same argument the prohibition makes about every named debt.
A line with no recorded origin and no household willing to admit it is the one case where the myth and the documented facts agree, and it is not claimed as evidence either way.
A belief with no progenitor cannot produce a funeral that means anything, so the rite had to be emptied until it was the only thing that could honestly be said.
The only tier where a law can be held apart from its effect and read, which is also the only tier where a retune could plausibly be argued about by somebody who was not there.
The clade vitrified at maturity, was defenseless against qi, and vanished in a single event when a world's physical law was retuned to raise material hardness.
An imprint is a group held at a value in a layer, so a body the law failed to hold is not the same thing as a body the law destroyed.
The college keeps the burnt list, and a doctrine that makes death reversible makes every entry in that book a provisional claim and therefore worthless as a record.
The Church keeps the register and the same reasoning applies to it, so two institutions with no shared deity have condemned the same sentence.
A line with no admitting household is the largest constituency of people the other records have already lost, and the appeal is entirely to the bereaved.
Houses culled their own branches to stop paying for siblings, so the population of the plains is full of exactly the people a reversible death would be addressed to.
Whether the seam was sealed or depleted is the same dispute at a smaller scale, and both accounts of it are held as mysteries rather than decided.
Form-Only Dao is Body Dao's form-permanence claim with the qi component removed; this heresy goes further and makes the removal the virtue rather than the loss.
A three-slot world spends its qi slot at the floor of its range, so a practitioner who cannot draw qi anyway arrives here independently of any teacher.
Qi imprinted at 0.1 works and resists every attempt to push it up, so the ceiling of this heresy is the world's floor and not its adherents' skill.
One charges for a seal and one regards every purchase as a concession, and neither congregation has ever explained itself to the other.
An absent group does not merely restrict practice, it invents one, and a body with nothing to spend on is a body nothing can take from.
Qi Dao is built on spending energy and this holds that every expenditure of qi is an avoidable loss, so the two are not two readings of one group.
Nothing above the mortal band has ever tested it against a realm-nineteen body, so it is unrefuted rather than proven and the hole is exactly there.
The most durable body anyone can build and the shortest-lived, which is the form-only position stated as a body rather than as a claim.
One worked face with its own forge, held for the rite and not for the market, worked by the congregation in rotation including the Binders.
Four decades of spoil stand uncarried on the seam floor and spatial law is unspent here, so the estate's real position is a heap it has already paid for.
Cement is the fee and the fee is the institution, so the estate's position is a claim on one exhausted deposit whose rate of fall is public.
Waste does not disperse on a tier with no spatial law, so a workable face is only workable once somebody has carried the heap off it by hand.
The guild works the flats and sells the tier's only dense material, and the temple holds the one face whose output is never sold, so neither can buy the other.
The estate is the standing answer to the exhaustion: a deposit kept for cement rather than for trade, which is the only arrangement that makes running out mean something.
With spatial law unwritten the heap stays where it is put, so the estate's defensible position is the ground it has already cleared and not any right to more.
Four sheds and one standing platform, built and maintained by the households that owe the rotation in stone cut on the ridge.
There is no warehouse on the pass, so a rotation's provisions must be carried in by hand, and that cost is what keeps the rotation honest.
Galehold collects the toll and maintains the crossing while the sheds keep warm the people who hold it; neither owns the other's function and each is indispensable.
With no elemental seat there is no forecast to staff against, so a shed standing empty for a month is cheaper than a garrison paid for a month nobody can predict.
Dense bodies cut and shift stone better than anything else on this ridge, so the sheds are built by the race that afterwards stands on them.
The flock occupies the worst hours of the crossing, and the sheds exist so that whoever is holding those hours has somewhere to stand while holding them.
No land, no buildings, no ore, no treasury and one register, survived four attempts to buy it by naming the holder alone.
The Vacancy Decree requires every office to be entered whether filled or not, and this is the body whose entry nobody contests.
The rule that the highest office may name a seat and may not take one is what turned the standing to certify a vacancy into something worth holding.
The notary exists precisely because vacancy could not be hidden, and an institution whose whole asset is a truthful list needs the office that made the list necessary.
No material asset means no raid worth mounting and no confession extractable, which is the counting houses' argument arriving a century later in clerical dress.
If vacancy is arithmetic rather than sacred this register has nothing left to be worth, which is the school's one serious argument against the faith.
The estate's largest annual expense is one period of naming every vacant seat aloud in the district below, which is expensive precisely where saying the word is.
Every socket in the temple's book opened, inspected, re-cemented and re-entered in front of the congregation, with the forge unhooded all night.
The only fixed calendar date the plains hold, because the frame seats no temporal law and the date is therefore purely an agreement between four calendars.
The observance is legal only because each socket is re-sealed in the same sitting, so the faith has to argue a distinction against its own prohibition.
The denomination attends and does not seal, standing at the back, which is the closest the two congregations have come to anything.
The night's draw is the largest single consumption of the year, which is why the deposit's rate of fall is a matter of public record rather than of private accounting.
Both hold a public reading in which the whole record is gone through in one sitting and nobody is permitted to leave early.
The observance is the initiation rite run against the whole book at once, which is the only way a seal nobody is permitted to open gets checked.
Every vacant seat read aloud in register order by a clerk, with no commentary and no petition from the floor, and the four unfillable named last.
A vacancy at this tier is a physical absence visible from the district below, so somebody has to stand in front of it once a period and say the word.
The failure this setting suffered is a slot that cannot be told from an empty one, and saying the word aloud once a period is the only available control on it.
The interval is the register's own period, which belongs to the court, so even the observance that names the court's vacancies runs on somebody else's clock.
The splinter holds that the reading is a comfort sold to the anxious; the church answers that comfort is not the objection and does not alter the practice.
The River Lantern is vacant because its heirs were culled rather than because a surplus exists, and the reading distinguishes the two states in public.
The register is the estate the observance spends, and its clerk is the only voice permitted to speak while the district below listens.
Once in a lifetime, entered in the register before a word is spoken, and never again, because a second oath is not permitted and does not need to be.
Sworn in the public forge with the furnace unhooded, because a self-binding nobody can witness is not a binding but a private promise.
The oath exists to bind the one body in the setting with the power to break the prohibition, and the prohibition is what gives the binding something to hold.
A Binder is buried as inventory with the socket recovered and consent not required, and that price is written into the oath before it is spoken.
Every Binder swears the oath before the forge and every one of them opens a socket once a year, which is the arrangement the congregation insists on reading as one act.
Houses culled branches rather than fund siblings, so an office that can only be entered once by lifetime is exactly the instrument a narrowed line can clear and nobody else.
The clerk will not answer, signal, nod or accept relief, including relief requested before the hour began.
The layer where fifteen imprints leave nine surplus and a single act of attention can be sustained past the end of any civilisation that has existed.
Temporal law readable to a hundred times is why the tier's resources are denominated in periods, and the oath's penalty is written in exactly those units.
The rite produces nothing observable, and this oath is the entire reason a silence can later be reported as an observation rather than as an absence.
A clerk honoured the oath once and then began a second hour anyway, so the faith's own account is that the dissolution clause was the problem and not the oath.
The only composition with real slack, and therefore the only one where holding an act of attention apart from its effect is possible at all.
Once per rotation, standing, with the pass behind the speaker, and no rite and no text because it is short enough to say over a mouthful of water.
A gate with a keeper who may refuse is a toll and not a pass, and this one clause is the reason the ridge is not what the Ninth Watch is.
The crossing is kept to the flock's dates, so the oath's only timetable is one no keeper on the ridge can move.
A stranger's first act on the plains is a transaction and their last is unrecorded, which is the arrangement this oath exists to refuse in one place.
Because no Keeper may refuse entry the toll is collected by the holder of the crossing and never by the faith, and that legal separation is what keeps both institutions standing.
A stand-in kinship on the plains keeps a household's obligations alive through somebody else's marriage, and the oath's no-refusal clause is the same rule stated for a shift.
A body that breathes volcanic grit stops at the eighth gate and cannot take the mind path, so the ridge can staff its worst hours with people who have no exit to be tempted by.
